data.name: UPA0001Title
data.value: Component lookup in per-frame method

data.name: UPA0001MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' performs a native component lookup on every call. Cache the result in a field during Awake or Start.

data.name: UPA0001Description
data.value: GetComponent and its related lookups cross the managed-native boundary and search the object's component list on every invocation. Inside methods that Unity runs every frame this cost repeats needlessly; resolve the component once in Awake or Start, store it in a field, and use the field on the hot path.

data.name: UPA0002Title
data.value: Object name or tag accessed in per-frame method

data.name: UPA0002MessageFormat
data.value: Reading '{0}' calls into native code and allocates a string on every access. Use CompareTag for comparisons, or cache the value.

data.name: UPA0002Description
data.value: The name and tag property getters call into Unity's native engine code and return a newly allocated managed string on every access. Inside methods that run every frame this produces avoidable garbage each frame. Use CompareTag for tag comparisons, or read the value once outside the hot path and cache it.

data.name: UPA0003Title
data.value: String-based shader or animator property access

data.name: UPA0003MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' resolves the string "{1}" to an ID on every call. Cache it in a static readonly int with Shader.PropertyToID / Animator.StringToHash.

data.name: UPA0003Description
data.value: Material, MaterialPropertyBlock, Shader, and Animator expose string-based overloads that hash the property or state name to an integer ID on every call. The integer overloads skip that conversion entirely. Resolving each name once with Shader.PropertyToID or Animator.StringToHash into a static readonly int removes the repeated conversion. Collecting those fields into one class per project is a common convention and works the same way, but it is a structure choice rather than part of the saving.

data.name: UPA0004Title
data.value: Instantiating accessor used in per-frame method

data.name: UPA0004MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' returns an instantiated copy that must be destroyed manually, and each access is a native call. Cache it in a field and release it in OnDestroy.

data.name: UPA0004Description
data.value: Renderer.material and MeshFilter.mesh duplicate the shared asset on first access and cache the copy; the caller owns that copy and must destroy it manually or it leaks. Every subsequent access is still a native property call, and Renderer.materials additionally returns a newly allocated array on each access. Cache the instance in a field outside the hot path and release it in OnDestroy, or use the shared* accessors when mutation of the shared asset is intended.

data.name: UPA0006Title
data.value: Reference type allocated in per-frame method

data.name: UPA0006MessageFormat
data.value: Allocating '{0}' on a per-frame path creates garbage every frame. Hoist the allocation out of the hot path, or reuse a cached or pooled instance.

data.name: UPA0006Description
data.value: Unity's garbage collector is non-generational: collection cost scales with the whole managed heap, and per-frame allocations steadily grow the garbage it must scan, surfacing as periodic frame spikes. This rule reports managed heap allocations on per-frame hot paths: object creations of reference types, array creations, and boxing conversions of value types. Hoist the allocation out of the hot path, reuse a cached or pooled instance, or use generic overloads to avoid boxing.

data.name: UPA0007Title
data.value: Capturing lambda in per-frame method

data.name: UPA0007MessageFormat
data.value: This lambda captures state and allocates a delegate and closure each time the enclosing code runs. Cache the delegate in a field, or rewrite it to avoid capturing.

data.name: UPA0007Description
data.value: A lambda or anonymous method that captures local variables, parameters, or this must allocate a closure object and a fresh delegate every time the enclosing code executes. On per-frame hot paths that garbage accumulates each frame. Lambdas that capture nothing are cached by the compiler and cost nothing after the first call, so they are not reported. Cache the delegate in a field during initialization, or restructure the lambda so it captures nothing.

data.name: UPA0008Title
data.value: stackalloc inside a loop

data.name: UPA0008MessageFormat
data.value: 'stackalloc' inside a loop reserves new stack memory on every iteration, and it is only reclaimed when the method returns. Hoist the buffer out of the loop and reuse it.

data.name: UPA0008Description
data.value: Memory reserved with stackalloc is released when the enclosing method returns, not when the current loop iteration or block ends. A stackalloc inside a loop therefore reserves a new region on every iteration while all previous regions stay live, which can overflow the stack. Hoist the buffer out of the loop and reuse it across iterations. A stackalloc at the top of a local function or lambda called from a loop is fine: that memory is reclaimed when the local function returns.

data.name: UPA0009Title
data.value: List Count not hoisted out of for loop

data.name: UPA0009MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}.Count' is re-read on every iteration of this loop. Hoist it into a local before the loop when the size does not change while iterating.

data.name: UPA0009Description
data.value: Reading List<T>.Count in a for-loop condition performs a property access on every iteration. When the list size does not change inside the loop, hoisting the count into a local before the loop removes that repeated read. Arrays are different: keep comparing against array.Length directly, because the JIT recognizes that form and eliminates bounds checks.

data.name: UPA0010Title
data.value: Raycast without explicit maxDistance or layerMask

data.name: UPA0010MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' without an explicit maxDistance and layerMask queries the entire scene across all layers. Pass both arguments to bound the query.

data.name: UPA0010Description
data.value: Physics.Raycast overloads that omit maxDistance query to infinity, and overloads that omit layerMask test every layer, including triggers and layers that were never meant to be hit. Both defaults make the query cost scale with the whole scene and are a common source of hard-to-debug false hits. Pass an explicit distance and mask; when hitting all layers really is intended, say so explicitly with ~0.

data.name: UPA0011Title
data.value: SetActive used to toggle UI visibility

data.name: UPA0011MessageFormat
data.value: Toggling '{0}' through SetActive deactivates the whole GameObject and forces canvas rebuild work when it is reactivated. Toggle the component's enabled property or drive a CanvasGroup's alpha instead.

data.name: UPA0011Description
data.value: Calling SetActive(false) on a UI element's GameObject deactivates the entire object; reactivating it runs OnEnable and forces the canvas to rebuild the element's geometry. For plain visibility toggling of a single UI graphic, disabling the component (enabled = false) or driving a CanvasGroup's alpha achieves the same visual result at a much lower reactivation cost. Only receivers statically typed as UI components are reported; toggling whole panels via SetActive is often intentional and is not.

data.name: UPA0012Title
data.value: TextMeshPro text assignment instead of SetText

data.name: UPA0012MessageFormat
data.value: Assigning '{0}.text' on a per-frame path stores a new string and dirties the text every frame. Use SetText with format arguments to write into the internal buffer instead.

data.name: UPA0012Description
data.value: Every assignment to a TextMeshPro text property stores the string and marks the text as dirty, triggering mesh regeneration. The common per-frame pattern also builds a fresh string first (value.ToString() or concatenation), allocating on every frame. The SetText overloads format numeric arguments directly into the component's internal buffer, avoiding the intermediate string allocation entirely.

data.name: UPA1000Title
data.value: Leaf class not sealed

data.name: UPA1000MessageFormat
data.value: This rule is deprecated: sealing '{0}' measured no gain that could be told apart from noise on IL2CPP.

data.name: UPA1000Description
data.value: Deprecated and off by default. This rule reported concrete classes with no derived types on the grounds that sealing them lets the runtime and IL2CPP replace virtual dispatch with direct calls. Measured against a probe with four derived classes and repeated eight times, sealed ran at 2.70 ns against 3.00 ns unsealed, a difference of 0.30 ns inside a spread of 1.28 ns, with the ordering reversing once. That is not a refutation of the premise; it is a measurement that cannot resolve it, and a rule whose payoff cannot be measured spends attention to buy something nobody can show. Sealing a leaf class is still reasonable design; it is no longer something this package warns about.

data.name: UPA0005Title
data.value: Direct UnityEngine.Debug logging call

data.name: UPA0005MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' is called directly. Route logging through a wrapper marked with [Conditional] so calls and their arguments are removed from release builds.

data.name: UPA0005Description
data.value: UnityEngine.Debug logging methods remain in release builds, and their argument expressions are still evaluated and allocated on every call. Routing log calls through a wrapper method marked with [System.Diagnostics.Conditional] lets the compiler remove the calls together with their argument expressions when the conditional symbol is not defined.

data.name: UPA1001Title
data.value: Non-exhaustive enum switch

data.name: UPA1001MessageFormat
data.value: Switch over '{0}' does not handle: {1}. Add the missing cases, or handle them deliberately in the default arm.

data.name: UPA1001Description
data.value: Adding an enum member without updating every switch over that enum is a common source of silent misbehavior: state machines skip the new state, item or damage types fall through unhandled. The compiler checks exhaustiveness only for switch expressions without a discard arm; this rule also covers switch statements, and can optionally keep reporting missing members even when a default arm exists. Flags enums and switches with when guards or non-constant patterns are not analyzed, and members sharing a value count as covered together.

data.name: UPA2000Title
data.value: String concatenation in per-frame method

data.name: UPA2000MessageFormat
data.value: String building on a per-frame path allocates a new string every frame. {0}

data.name: UPA2000Description
data.value: String concatenation, += appends, and string interpolation each allocate a new string on every execution. Inside methods that Unity runs every frame this produces avoidable garbage each frame. Cache strings that do not change, build changing ones with a reusable StringBuilder outside the hot path, or use ZString to format without intermediate string allocations when it is available.

data.name: UPA2000AdviceDefault
data.value: Cache the string, or build it with a reusable StringBuilder outside the hot path.

data.name: UPA2000AdviceZString
data.value: Use ZString to format without intermediate string allocations.

data.name: UPA0013Title
data.value: System.Linq usage

data.name: UPA0013MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' allocates enumerators and often intermediate collections. Use a loop or a non-allocating alternative on performance-sensitive paths.

data.name: UPA0013Description
data.value: LINQ operators allocate enumerator objects, delegate instances, and often intermediate collections on every evaluation. That cost is acceptable in general .NET code but conflicts with the low-allocation discipline of performance-sensitive Unity projects. This opinionated rule reports every call to a System.Linq.Enumerable or System.Linq.Queryable extension method, including query syntax; it is disabled by default and intended to be enabled by projects that ban LINQ as a stack choice.

data.name: UPA2010Title
data.value: User-authored async method returns Task

data.name: UPA2010MessageFormat
data.value: Async method '{0}' returns Task, which allocates on every invocation. With UniTask referenced, return UniTask instead to avoid the allocations.

data.name: UPA2010Description
data.value: Every invocation of an async method that returns Task or Task<T> allocates the Task object, and awaits that yield allocate state-machine boxes. UniTask provides allocation-free equivalents designed for Unity's player loop. This rule runs only in assemblies that reference UniTask and reports user-authored async method declarations returning Task; overrides, interface implementations, and async lambdas are excluded because their signatures cannot be changed unilaterally.

data.name: UPA2011Title
data.value: Coroutine IEnumerator Unity message or method

data.name: UPA2011MessageFormat
data.value: Coroutine '{0}' allocates its enumerator state machine each time it starts, and each StartCoroutine call allocates a Coroutine handle. Convert it to an async UniTask or UniTaskVoid method instead.

data.name: UPA2011Description
data.value: A coroutine method allocates its compiler-generated enumerator state machine on every start, and each StartCoroutine call additionally allocates a Coroutine handle object; yielded values that are value types are boxed. Async UniTask methods avoid these repeated allocations, and logic that never yields can be a plain method. This rule runs only when the assembly references UniTask, so the suggested rewrite is always available. Methods returning IEnumerator<T> are treated as data iteration and not reported.

data.name: UPA2012Title
data.value: Async void or unawaited fire-and-forget

data.name: UPA2012MessageFormatAsyncVoid
data.value: '{0}' is async void: exceptions escape every caller and completion cannot be observed. {1}

data.name: UPA2012MessageFormatFireAndForget
data.value: The result of '{0}' is discarded, so its exceptions are silently lost. {1}

data.name: UPA2012Description
data.value: Exceptions thrown by an async void method cannot be caught by any caller and its completion cannot be observed; a Task or UniTask whose result is discarded at the call site silently swallows its exceptions the same way. Both are debugging black holes. Return an awaitable type and observe it at the call sites, or make fire-and-forget explicit — with UniTask, return UniTaskVoid and call Forget. Event-handler-signature async void methods and explicit discard assignments are excluded as established conventions.

data.name: UPA2012AdviceAsyncVoidDefault
data.value: Return Task instead, and await or store it at the call sites.

data.name: UPA2012AdviceAsyncVoidUniTask
data.value: Return UniTaskVoid and call Forget, or return UniTask.

data.name: UPA2012AdviceFireAndForgetDefault
data.value: Await it, or store the task and observe its completion.

data.name: UPA2012AdviceFireAndForgetUniTask
data.value: Await it, or make fire-and-forget explicit with Forget.

data.name: UPA2021Title
data.value: Public Action event used for observable state

data.name: UPA2021MessageFormat
data.value: Public event '{0}' models observable state with a plain Action. With R3 referenced, expose a ReactiveProperty or Observable for composable, disposable subscriptions instead.

data.name: UPA2021Description
data.value: A public event of the System.Action family is the idiomatic shape for state-change notification, but plain events offer no composition, no current-value semantics, and easy-to-leak manual unsubscription. R3's ReactiveProperty and Observable provide composable, disposable subscriptions with explicit ordering. This rule runs only in assemblies that reference R3; EventHandler-convention events, non-public events, custom delegate types, and plain Action fields are not reported.

data.name: UPA0014Title
data.value: Scene-search API call in per-frame method

data.name: UPA0014MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' searches the scene on every call and is not intended for per-frame use. Resolve the reference once in Awake or Start and cache it in a field.

data.name: UPA0014Description
data.value: GameObject.Find and the Object.FindObjectOfType/FindObjectsByType family walk the scene or all loaded objects on every call, and Unity's documentation warns against calling them every frame. Resolve the reference once in Awake or Start and cache it in a field, or restructure the code around direct references. Only per-frame Unity messages and methods marked with a hot-path attribute are checked.

data.name: UPA0015Title
data.value: Camera.main accessed in per-frame method

data.name: UPA0015MessageFormat
data.value: 'Camera.main' performs a lookup comparable to GetComponent on every access. Cache the camera in a field during Awake or Start.

data.name: UPA0015Description
data.value: Accessing Camera.main has a small CPU overhead comparable to calling GameObject.GetComponent. Unity 2020.2 and later cache the main-camera lookup internally, so the residual cost is small — this rule therefore reports at Info level. Where CPU performance matters, cache the camera in a field during Awake or Start. Only per-frame Unity messages and methods marked with a hot-path attribute are checked.

data.name: UPA0016Title
data.value: SendMessage / BroadcastMessage call

data.name: UPA0016MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' uses reflection-based message dispatch, which is orders of magnitude slower than a direct call. Call the method directly, or use an interface or UnityEvent.

data.name: UPA0016Description
data.value: SendMessage, SendMessageUpwards, and BroadcastMessage dispatch by reflection, which can be orders of magnitude slower than a direct method call and turns missing-method mistakes into silent runtime failures. Call the target method directly, or decouple the caller with an interface or a UnityEvent. This rule reports everywhere, not just on per-frame hot paths.

data.name: UPA0018Title
data.value: Allocating array-returning Unity API in per-frame method

data.name: UPA0018MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' returns a newly allocated array every time it runs. Use {1} instead.

data.name: UPA0018Description
data.value: Unity APIs that return arrays create a new copy of the array every time they run. This rule checks a closed deny-list of UnityEngine members with documented non-allocating counterparts: Input.touches (use touchCount with GetTouch), Animator.parameters (use parameterCount with GetParameter), Animator.GetCurrentAnimatorClipInfo (use the List overload), Renderer.sharedMaterials (use GetSharedMaterials with a cached List), Camera.allCameras (use GetAllCameras with a preallocated array), and the Texture2D pixel readers GetPixels, GetPixels32 and the non-generic GetRawTextureData (use the generic GetRawTextureData overload, which returns a NativeArray view). Known-allocating BCL members belong to UPA0030 instead. Physics queries, Mesh array properties and the GetComponents overloads are deliberately excluded — other rules own those cases. Only per-frame Unity messages and methods marked with a hot-path attribute are checked.

data.name: UPA0017Title
data.value: Array-returning GetComponents overload in per-frame method

data.name: UPA0017MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' allocates a new array on every call. Use the List<T> overload with a list cached in a field instead.

data.name: UPA0017Description
data.value: The array-returning GetComponents, GetComponentsInChildren, and GetComponentsInParent overloads allocate a fresh array on every call, like all Unity APIs that return arrays. The List<T> overloads fill a caller-provided list instead, avoiding the allocation when the list is cached in a field. There is no automatic fix — introducing the reusable list field is a type-level change. Only per-frame Unity messages and methods marked with a hot-path attribute are checked; the singular GetComponent lookups are UPA0001's territory.

data.name: UPA0019Title
data.value: Boxed value yielded from coroutine

data.name: UPA0019MessageFormat
data.value: Yielding '{0}' boxes the value on every resume, and Unity treats it the same as null. Yield null to wait one frame.

data.name: UPA0019Description
data.value: In a MonoBehaviour coroutine (a method returning the non-generic IEnumerator), yielding a value type boxes it on every resume, and Unity treats any boxed value that is not a YieldInstruction the same as null — a one-frame wait. Yielding null does not allocate. YieldInstruction and CustomYieldInstruction yields are normal usage, and IEnumerator methods on non-MonoBehaviour types are not reported because their yielded values may carry meaning.

data.name: UPA0020Title
data.value: Lambda in WaitUntil / WaitWhile construction

data.name: UPA0020MessageFormat
data.value: Constructing this {0} with a lambda allocates the delegate (and any closure) each time this code runs. Cache the yield instruction and its predicate in fields.

data.name: UPA0020Description
data.value: Constructing WaitUntil or WaitWhile with a lambda allocates the delegate and any captured closure on every construction; Unity's coroutine guidance recommends caching commonly reused yield instructions and avoiding lambdas in WaitUntil and WaitWhile. The rule performs no flow analysis, so a construction that provably runs once (for example in a field initializer) still reports — suppress locally or cache the predicate in a field. Disabled by default.

data.name: UPA0021Title
data.value: magnitude or Distance compared where sqrMagnitude suffices

data.name: UPA0021MessageFormat
data.value: Comparing '{0}' computes a square root. Compare sqrMagnitude against the squared threshold instead.

data.name: UPA0021Description
data.value: The magnitude property and the Vector Distance methods compute a square root. When the result is only compared against a threshold, comparing sqrMagnitude against the squared threshold is equivalent and much faster. Comparisons with a magnitude or Distance expression on both sides are not reported — rewriting those brings no gain. The code fix applies only when the other side is a plain numeric literal; other thresholds must be squared by hand.

data.name: UPA0022Title
data.value: Enum.HasFlag in per-frame method

data.name: UPA0022MessageFormat
data.value: This rule is deprecated: 'HasFlag' does not box and is not slower than a bitwise check on any supported Unity runtime.

data.name: UPA0022Description
data.value: Deprecated and off by default. This rule reported Enum.HasFlag on the grounds that it boxes its operands. It does not: Mono has replaced the same-type call with a bitwise AND since 4.0 and IL2CPP since Unity 2021.2, measured at no allocation on every supported configuration, and on IL2CPP the call runs faster than the rewrite this rule used to suggest. The argument box IL emits goes with the call for a plain load - a constant, local, parameter, field or property - and survives only when a conditional is written inline at the call site, which UPA0006 reports.

data.name: UPA0023Title
data.value: OnGUI declared in player code

data.name: UPA0023MessageFormat
data.value: 'OnGUI' runs IMGUI every frame and is not intended for in-game interfaces. Use UI Toolkit or uGUI for player UI, or gate debug overlays behind a define.

data.name: UPA0023Description
data.value: OnGUI runs Unity's immediate-mode GUI system every frame, often multiple times per frame, and IMGUI is not generally intended for normal in-game user interfaces — its supported uses are debug displays, tooling, and editor extensions. Use UI Toolkit or uGUI for player UI, or gate debug overlays behind a define. Assemblies that reference UnityEditor are not checked. Info severity and disabled by default: development-time overlays are legitimate and common.

data.name: UPA0024Title
data.value: Resources.Load in per-frame method

data.name: UPA0024MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' performs an asset lookup and load on every call. Load the asset once outside the hot path and cache the reference.

data.name: UPA0024Description
data.value: Resources.Load, LoadAll, and LoadAsync perform an asset lookup and load on every call, and Unity's guidance discourages relying on the Resources system in general; calling it per frame compounds the cost. Load the asset once outside the hot path and cache the reference. The rule is disabled by default and limited to per-frame hot paths — enable it in projects that still use Resources folders.

data.name: UPA0025Title
data.value: Finalizer declared in runtime code

data.name: UPA0025MessageFormat
data.value: Finalizers delay memory reclamation across garbage collections and run on the finalizer thread. Implement IDisposable and remove the finalizer.

data.name: UPA0025Description
data.value: Unity's programming best practices say not to use C# finalizers in runtime code: a finalizable object survives at least one extra garbage-collection cycle before its memory is reclaimed, the finalizer runs on a dedicated thread with no ordering guarantees, and the extra bookkeeping makes collection pauses less predictable. Implement IDisposable for deterministic cleanup and remove the finalizer. Assemblies that reference UnityEditor are not checked.

data.name: UPA0026Title
data.value: Value type boxed by inherited method call

data.name: UPA0026MessageFormat
data.value: 'GetType' is inherited from Object, so calling it on a value type boxes the receiver. The type is known at compile time — use typeof instead.

data.name: UPA0026Description
data.value: GetType is declared on Object and cannot be overridden, so calling it on a struct or enum boxes the receiver to reach it. The type is a compile-time fact, so typeof gives the same answer for nothing. Only per-frame Unity messages and methods marked with a hot-path attribute are checked. ToString, GetHashCode and Equals(object) were reported here until they were measured on IL2CPP and found to box no receiver.

data.name: UPA2030Title
data.value: Tween created in per-frame method

data.name: UPA2030MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' creates a new tween every frame, allocating and churning DOTween's active list. Create the tween once and reuse it with SetAutoKill(false) and Restart or ChangeEndValue.

data.name: UPA2030Description
data.value: Every tween-creating call (DOMove and the other shortcuts, DOTween.To, DOTween.Sequence) allocates a tween and registers it in DOTween's active list; doing this in a per-frame method churns both. DOTween's own API supports reuse: create the tween once, disable auto-kill with SetAutoKill(false), and drive it with Restart or ChangeEndValue. Configuration calls on an existing tween (SetLoops, SetEase, ...) are not reported — a fluent chain reports once, at its creation root. This rule runs only in assemblies that reference DOTween.

data.name: UPA2031Title
data.value: Discarded infinite tween without SetLink

data.name: UPA2031MessageFormat
data.value: This infinite tween is discarded and has no SetLink, so it can never be killed and outlives its target. Store the tween and kill it in OnDestroy, or add SetLink(gameObject).

data.name: UPA2031Description
data.value: DOTween's auto-kill fires when a tween completes, and a tween with SetLoops(-1) never completes. When such a tween is neither stored nor linked, no code path can kill it: it keeps running after its target is destroyed, which wastes work and surfaces as errors or leaks. Store the tween in a field and kill it in OnDestroy, or bind its lifetime with SetLink(gameObject). Chains whose result is assigned, passed on, or carrying a SetLink are not reported. This rule runs only in assemblies that reference DOTween.

data.name: UPA2032Title
data.value: String tween ID

data.name: UPA2032MessageFormat
data.value: String tween IDs are the slowest of the fast filter options. Prefer an int ID, or filter by the target reference.

data.name: UPA2032Description
data.value: DOTween's filtered operations (DOTween.Kill, Play, Pause, ...) are fastest when filtering by an ID, and DOTween's documentation notes that int IDs are faster than string IDs. This rule reports string arguments to SetId and to the static filtered operations. Info severity: the cost only matters when filtered operations run often. This rule runs only in assemblies that reference DOTween.

data.name: UPA3000Title
data.value: Threading API unsupported on WebGL

data.name: UPA3000MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' requires threads, which Unity WebGL builds do not support. Use async/await on the main thread, coroutines, or the Job System.

data.name: UPA3000Description
data.value: Unity WebGL builds run on a single thread: thread creation, thread-pool scheduling, and blocking synchronization primitives either throw or hang at runtime. Task.Run and TaskFactory.StartNew schedule onto the thread pool, and Task.Delay relies on timer machinery known not to complete on WebGL. Plain async/await on the main thread, coroutines, lock, Interlocked, and CancellationToken remain usable. This rule runs only in compilations that define UPA_TARGET_WEBGL.

data.name: UPA3001Title
data.value: Sockets API unsupported on WebGL

data.name: UPA3001MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' uses sockets, which Unity WebGL builds do not support. Use UnityWebRequest or a WebSocket solution instead.

data.name: UPA3001Description
data.value: Browsers do not expose raw socket access, so System.Net.Sockets types fail at runtime in Unity WebGL builds. Use UnityWebRequest for HTTP traffic or a WebSocket-based solution for persistent connections. This rule runs only in compilations that define UPA_TARGET_WEBGL.

data.name: UPA3002Title
data.value: Synchronous file IO unsupported on WebGL

data.name: UPA3002MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' performs synchronous file IO, which Unity WebGL builds do not support. Persist data with PlayerPrefs or asynchronous storage APIs instead.

data.name: UPA3002Description
data.value: Unity WebGL builds have no real file system: File and Directory static methods and FileStream construction fail or silently misbehave against the browser's virtual file system. Persist data with PlayerPrefs or asynchronous storage APIs. Path operations are pure string manipulation and MemoryStream is in-memory, so both remain usable. This rule runs only in compilations that define UPA_TARGET_WEBGL.

data.name: UPA3003Title
data.value: Process API unsupported on WebGL

data.name: UPA3003MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' launches processes, which Unity WebGL builds do not support. Remove or platform-gate this code.

data.name: UPA3003Description
data.value: Browsers cannot launch or inspect operating-system processes, so System.Diagnostics.Process fails at runtime in Unity WebGL builds. Remove the usage or gate it behind a platform define for the targets that support it. This rule runs only in compilations that define UPA_TARGET_WEBGL.

data.name: UPA3004Title
data.value: Blocking wait on asynchronous operation

data.name: UPA3004MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' blocks the main thread until an asynchronous operation completes, which deadlocks single-threaded Unity WebGL players. Await the operation instead of waiting synchronously.

data.name: UPA3004Description
data.value: Unity WebGL players run on a single thread: when the main thread blocks waiting for an asynchronous operation, the continuation that would complete the operation can never run, so the application freezes rather than slows down. This applies to AsyncOperationHandle.WaitForCompletion, Task.Wait, Task.WaitAll, Task.WaitAny, Task<TResult>.Result and the GetAwaiter().GetResult() idiom, patterns that often appear to work on desktop platforms where a thread pool exists. Await the operation instead. This rule runs only in compilations that define UPA_TARGET_WEBGL.

data.name: UPA0027Title
data.value: Params array allocated at call site

data.name: UPA0027MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' resolves to its params overload here, allocating a {1}[] on every call. Use a fixed-arity overload, hoist the array to a field, or nest the calls.

data.name: UPA0027MessageFormatBoxing
data.value: '{0}' resolves to its params object[] overload here, allocating an array and boxing {1} value-type argument(s) on every call. Convert the arguments yourself, or use an overload that does not take object.

data.name: UPA0028Title
data.value: Value type used as collection key without IEquatable

data.name: UPA0028MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' is used as a collection key but implements neither IEquatable<{0}> nor an override of GetHashCode. Every comparison boxes and falls back to reflection.

data.name: UPA0028MessageFormatEquatable
data.value: '{0}' is used as a collection key without implementing IEquatable<{0}>. EqualityComparer<{0}>.Default will box on every comparison.

data.name: UPA0028MessageFormatHashCode
data.value: '{0}' is used as a collection key without overriding GetHashCode. ValueType.GetHashCode uses reflection.

data.name: UPA0028Description
data.value: EqualityComparer<T>.Default chooses its implementation from the type: when T implements IEquatable<T> it calls the typed Equals directly, and otherwise it calls object.Equals(object), which boxes both operands on every comparison. When the struct also does not override Equals, the inherited ValueType.Equals compares field by field through reflection. GetHashCode behaves the same way, so both members are needed — implementing only one still leaves a cost. Enums are not reported: measurement across Mono and IL2CPP confirms the runtime has non-boxing comparers for them. Type parameters are not reported either, since the answer depends on the instantiated type. Unlike CA1815, this rule fires only where the struct is actually used as a key, so consider setting CA1815 to none when this rule is enabled.

data.name: UPA0029Title
data.value: Sequential Add replaceable with AddRange

data.name: UPA0029MessageFormat
data.value: This loop adds elements one at a time, which can reallocate the backing array several times. Use AddRange to size the buffer once.

data.name: UPA0029Description
data.value: List<T> grows by doubling: adding N elements one at a time can reallocate and copy the backing array O(log N) times. AddRange reserves the space up front instead — but only when the source implements ICollection<T>, which is what lets it ask how many elements are coming. For a plain IEnumerable<T>, such as a LINQ query or an iterator method, AddRange falls back to adding one at a time and there is nothing to gain, so this rule checks the source type rather than suggesting the swap unconditionally. Only loops whose body is a single Add of the iteration element are reported: a projection, a filter or an extra statement changes the meaning, and AddRange would not reproduce it. Set upa_addrange_hot_path_only to true to narrow the rule to per-frame code.

data.name: UPA0030Title
data.value: Known-allocating BCL API in per-frame method

data.name: UPA0030MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' allocates a new {1} on every call. {2}

data.name: UPA0030MessageFormatConditional
data.value: '{0}' allocates a new {1} whenever it has work to do. {2}

data.name: UPA0030Description
data.value: Whether an arbitrary method allocates cannot be decided without escape analysis across method boundaries, so this rule does not try: it checks a closed list of BCL members whose allocation is a documented, measured fact. The list covers the string operations that return a new instance (Split, ToCharArray, Substring, ToLower, ToLowerInvariant, ToUpper, ToUpperInvariant, Trim, TrimStart, TrimEnd) and the enum reflection helpers that return a new array on every call (Enum.GetValues, Enum.GetNames). Trim and its variants return the original instance when there is nothing to trim, so a reported call may cost nothing in practice; the rule cannot know the contents of the string. UnityEngine members with the same problem are reported by UPA0018 instead, so no call is reported twice. Only per-frame Unity messages and methods marked with a hot-path attribute are checked.

data.name: UPA0031Title
data.value: Instantiate or Destroy in per-frame method

data.name: UPA0031MessageFormat
data.value: '{0}' is instantiated inside a per-frame method. If this runs on more than the occasional frame, take one from a pool and return it when done.

data.name: UPA0031MessageFormatDestroy
data.value: '{0}' is destroyed inside a per-frame method, and destroying queues the object for collection rather than freeing it. If this runs on more than the occasional frame, return it to a pool instead.

data.name: UPA0031Description
data.value: Creating and destroying objects every frame produces garbage the collector must reclaim, and Unity object construction is not cheap. Reuse instances from a pool instead.

data.name: UPA0027Description
data.value: A params parameter can be called in two ways. Passing an array uses normal form, where the allocation is visible and under the caller's control. Passing the elements directly uses expanded form, where the compiler creates a new array at the call site on every call — nothing in the source says so. Mathf.Max and Mathf.Min are the common case in Unity, since only arity-2 overloads exist and a third argument silently switches to the params overload; string.Format, string.Concat, string.Join, Path.Combine and Debug.LogFormat behave the same way past their fixed-arity overloads. When the parameter is params object[], each value-type argument boxes on top of the array allocation. Zero-argument calls are not reported: those compile to Array.Empty and allocate nothing. Only per-frame Unity messages and methods marked with a hot-path attribute are checked.
